title: rorca-enrich-context-retrieval

userStories.title: Replace enrich route inline retrieval cascade with retrieveContext() per story
userStories.description: The POST /api/specs/:id/enrich route in backend/src/routes/specs.ts currently implements its own inline 4-layer retrieval cascade that is disconnected from memory-router.ts. This story replaces that inline logic with per-story calls to retrieveContext(workspaceId, story.title + ' ' + story.description, { maxTokens: 2000, includeGraph: true }) from backend/src/lib/memory-router.ts. Each story in the spec gets its own semantically matched context via cosine similarity instead of the same 10 recency-ordered memories. Aggregate cagHits, ragHits, graphHits, and latencyMs across all per-story calls. After all stories are processed, write a context_summary_json entry to spec_generation_logs using the canonical ContextSummary schema: { directionLayers: [...], skills: [...], memory: { count, tier, cagHits, ragHits, graphHits, latencyMs }, tokenBudget, flags }. Set the retrieval_method column to the highest tier used across all story calls (graph > rag > cag > direction_only). The existing inline pgvector/AGE/tsvector/direction-only code block must be fully removed from the enrich route handler — no dead code left behind.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:id/enrich no longer contains any inline SQL queries against pgvector, tsvector, or AGE — all retrieval is delegated to memory-router.ts retrieveContext()

Each userStory in the spec receives its own retrieveContext(workspaceId, story.title + ' ' + story.description, { maxTokens: 2000, includeGraph: true }) call, producing semantically different context per story based on cosine similarity
cagHits in the aggregated context_summary_json is non-zero when memory-router.ts CAG cache contains relevant entries (i.e., the cache is actually consulted via memory-router.ts, not bypassed)

After enrichment, a row is inserted into spec_generation_logs with context_summary_json matching the ContextSummary schema shape used by the generate route: { directionLayers, skills, memory: { count, tier, cagHits, ragHits, graphHits, latencyMs }, tokenBudget, flags }

retrieval_method column in spec_generation_logs is set to 'graph' if any story call used AGE traversal, 'rag' if pgvector/tsvector was used, 'cag' if only cache was used, or 'direction_only' as fallback — reflecting the highest tier actually used across all per-story calls

userStories.title: Show ContextSummaryCard in Context tab for enriched specs
userStories.description: After US-001 writes context_summary_json to spec_generation_logs for enriched specs, the frontend SpecDetailSlideOver Context tab must render the same rich ContextSummaryCard component that is already shown for generated specs. Currently the Context tab either shows nothing or a fallback empty state for specs that were enriched rather than generated. This story ensures the Context tab fetches the spec_generation_logs entry for the enrich operation (trigger_type = 'enrich' or equivalent) and passes context_summary_json to the existing ContextSummaryCard component. The card must display: direction layers count, skills matched, memory tier (cag/rag/graph/direction_only), cagHits, ragHits, graphHits, latencyMs, tokenBudget, and flags. No new UI components should be created — reuse the existing ContextSummaryCard. If multiple log entries exist (e.g., both a generate and a later enrich), show the most recent one. Add a label or badge indicating whether the context came from 'Generated' or 'Enriched' to distinguish the source.
acceptanceCriteria: The Context tab in SpecDetailSlideOver for a spec that has been enriched (but not generated via Rorca) renders ContextSummaryCard with data from the enrich operation's spec_generation_logs row — no empty state or null render
ContextSummaryCard shows memory.cagHits, memory.ragHits, memory.graphHits, and memory.latencyMs sourced from the aggregated per-story retrieveContext() calls written by US-001

When a spec has both a 'generate' log entry and a later 'enrich' log entry, the Context tab displays the most recent entry and shows a 'Enriched' badge (e.g., amber label) next to the timestamp to distinguish it from a 'Generated' entry (green label)
No new ContextSummaryCard component is introduced — the existing component used by the generate flow is reused without duplication

=== GLOBAL STANDARDS (L1) ===
test: true

=== PROJECT CONTEXT (L3) ===
name: rorca
type: web-app
purpose: >-
  AI spec orchestration and pipeline management platform. Converts plain-English briefs
  into structured specs (user stories with acceptance criteria), then executes each story
  as an isolated agent subprocess with full tool access — bash, edit, read, write, glob, grep.
  Tracks progress in real time via SSE/WAL events. Supports three execution engines:
  claude --print (Claude subscription), opencode run (75+ providers), codex (ChatGPT subscription).

stack:
  - React 18
  - TypeScript (strict)
  - Vite 5
  - Tailwind CSS 3
  - xterm.js (@xterm/xterm)
  - react-router-dom v7
  - Express.js
  - PostgreSQL 16 (pg Pool, pgvector, Apache AGE)
  - Node.js >= 20
  - Vitest (frontend tests)
  - Jest (backend tests)
  - Playwright (E2E)
  - Docker Compose

key_modules:
  - src/panels/ — 5 primary panels (SpecsPanel, RunsPanel, AnalyticsPanel, DirectionPanel, SettingsPanel)
  - src/components/ — Shared UI (Shell, Sidebar, RunTerminal, SpecDetailSlideOver, CommandPalette)
  - src/contexts/ — WorkspaceContext, AuthContext, ThemeContext, ToastContext
  - backend/src/routes/ — 32 Express route files (specs, pipeline, workspaces, direction, skills, etc.)
  - backend/src/lib/ — Core services (execution-engine, sse-hub, direction-stack, llm-client, context-router, workspace-echolocation)
  - backend/src/db/ — PostgreSQL Pool, pg-index.ts migration runner, pg-migrations/ (001–049)
  - backend/src/mcp/ — MCP stdio server (5 tools, HTTP transport target)
  - forge/ — run-loop.sh (bash fallback), self-register.ts, spec JSON files
  - packs/ — Convention pack directory (planned)

ports:
  frontend: 5210
  backend: 3030
  finops_sim: 5200

constraints:
  - Backend requires manual restart (no hot-reload via tsx)
  - Auth middleware globally bypassed — local single-user tool
  - WAL wal_events.ts column is ts not created_at
  - spec.id is filename slug — never use specName for paths
  - pg uses numbered placeholders $1/$2 not ?
  - chatComplete returns ChatResult.text — not a plain string

deployment_target: self-hosted (npm run dev locally), Docker Compose, future binary via bun build --compile

integrations:
  - GitHub OAuth + webhooks (partially built)
  - Linear (planned)
  - Vercel (planned)
  - Slack (planned)
  - Claude Code MCP (stdio + HTTP transport)
  - skills.sh registry

=== PROJECT MEMORY (Git History) ===
```yaml
architectural_decisions:
  - description: "Direction stack now 6-layer: L0 (convention packs) → L1 (global eng principles) → L2 (domain) → L3 (project) → L4 (spec brief) → L5 (story annotations). Lower layers override higher (CSS specificity model)."
    evidence: "Convention pack system commit — L0 layer introduced for community-driven conventions below user-defined L1-L5"
  
  - description: "Single execution engine (execution-engine.ts) replaces all bash/TypeScript variants. Supports 3 agent types (claude, opencode, codex) with shared tool set (edit, bash, read, write, glob, grep, webfetch, websearch)."
    evidence: "run-loop.ts (1780 lines) deleted — execution-engine.ts is single source of truth"
  
  - description: "PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector + Apache AGE replaces SQLite. Enables vector search, graph queries, concurrent writes. Port 5433 to avoid user's local Postgres on 5432."
    evidence: "rorca-postgres-migration.json spec created, better-sqlite3 → pg for distribution compatibility (bun build --compile breaks on native addons)"
  
  - description: "Skills are L0 context (below L1-L5 direction stack). LLM matches skills per story during spec generation. No embeddings — single LLM call with skill catalog + MEMORY.md + AGENTS.md + story text outputs relevance scores (1-10) + reasoning."
    evidence: "LLM-driven skill matching commits — piggybacks on spec generation, zero extra API cost. Signal hierarchy: MEMORY.md (strongest) → AGENTS.md → story text → domain L2"
  
  - description: "Skills dual-injected: Claude via .claude/skills/ auto-discovery (native), OpenCode/Codex via buildPrompt() manual injection. Token budgeting through enforceBudget() sorted by LLM relevance score."
    evidence: "react.md + tailwind.md added to both .claude/skills/ and .rorca/skills/ for dual injection"
  
  - description: "Convention packs = frameworks for AI development. Directory structure: packs/<name>/ with direction/, personas/, conventions/, templates/, scaffold/, AGENTS.md. Installed packs populate .rorca/ + direction stack + project scaffold."
    evidence: "Convention pack system + pack_registry table (migration 040) + API routes for install/fork/uninstall"
  
  - description: "Greenfield vs Brownfield onboarding: Greenfield = top-down convention injection from packs. Brownfield = bottom-up convention extraction (agent scans codebase → generates L3 + CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md → human approval via convention_proposals table)."
    evidence: "Convention inference agent + convention_proposals table (migration 040) for brownfield workflow"
  
  - description: "Agent persona system: Stories support 'persona' + 'reviewers' fields. Personas stored in .rorca/personas/ with 4 categories (_primary/, _adversarial/, _specialist/, _review/). buildPrompt() injects persona markdown before story execution."
    evidence: "15 default personas added (architect, pm, lead-dev, red-team, assumption-buster, devils-advocate, spec-writer, spec-verifier, best-practices, etc.)"
  
  - description: "Multi-pass spec generation pipeline: PM → Spec Writer → UX Designer → Best Practices → Adversarial → Verifier. Each pass refines previous output. Goal: exhaustive specs (every state/edge case/button label explicit, 20-50K words so 'a blind person can implement')."
    evidence: "Multi-pass spec generation commits + spec_versions table for version history per pass"
  
  - description: "Distribution via bun build --compile (standalone binary, no source visible, no runtime dependency). Postgres 16 + pgvector + AGE downloaded on first run to ~/.rorca/postgres/ (Prisma/Playwright pattern). Install: curl -fsSL https://get.rorca.app | sh"
    evidence: "rorca-distribution.json spec created, bin/rorca.ts CLI added with 'rorca start' and 'rorca init'"
  
  - description: "Per-story model override: UserStory interface extended with optional 'model' field. Precedence: story.model > run-level --model > workspace L3 preferred_model > DEFAULT_MODEL. Escalation cascade (Haiku→Sonnet→Opus) still applies on top."
    evidence: "Per-story model routing commit — execution-engine.ts reads story.model before spawning subprocess"
  
  - description: "Skills routed through existing context router (no separate routing block in config.json). Skills are files — micromatch path rules + priority + enforceBudget() applies. Rejected: separate skills routing (duplicates work), bulk install 30+ skills (context pollution), embedding similarity search (replaced by LLM reasoning)."
    evidence: "Skills treated as files commit — context-router.ts unchanged, skills just added to routing table"

bug_patterns:
  - pattern: "Auto-stash runtime files (.rorca/run-state.json, progress.txt, *.jsonl) caused merge conflicts during wave execution."
    example: ".gitignore updated with patterns for run-state.json, progress.txt, *.jsonl, .DS_Store"
  
  - pattern: "Native C++ addons (better-sqlite3) break bun build --compile. Blocked standalone binary distribution."
    example: "PostgreSQL migration prerequisite for distribution — pg is pure JS, works with bun compile"

conventions:
  - rule: "Direction stack precedence: lower layer number overrides higher (L0 < L1 < L2 < L3 < L4 < L5). L0 = convention packs (community defaults), L1-L3 = user-defined, L4-L5 = spec-specific."
  
  - rule: "Persona categories use underscore prefix directories: _primary/, _adversarial/, _specialist/, _review/. Persona files are markdown with YAML frontmatter."
  
  - rule: "Skills dual-saved: .rorca/skills/ (Rorca internal) + .claude/skills/ (Claude CLI auto-discovery). Both copies kept in sync during install/uninstall."
  
  - rule: "Convention packs must have: pack.json (metadata), direction/, personas/, conventions/, templates/, scaffold/, AGENTS.md. Pack loader validates structure before install."
  
  - rule: "LLM skill matching output format: suggestedSkills array per story with { name, relevanceScore (1-10), reason (cites MEMORY.md/AGENTS.md/L2) }."
  
  - rule: "Skill content injection: Claude = noop (auto-discovered), OpenCode/Codex = buildPrompt() reads .rorca/skills/<name>.md + injects into prompt before story execution."
  
  - rule: "Convention proposals (brownfield extraction) stored in convention_proposals table with status: pending/approved/rejected. Human reviews before applying to direction_layers or writing CLAUDE.md."
  
  - rule: "Postgres port 5433 (not 5432) to avoid conflict with user's local Postgres. ~/.rorca/postgres/ for bundled Postgres data directory."
  
  - rule: "Per-story model override precedence: story.model > run --model flag > workspace L3 preferred_model > DEFAULT_MODEL. Escalation (Haiku→Sonnet→Opus) still applies after selection."
  
  - rule: "CLI commands: 'rorca start' (Express + built frontend on :3030), 'rorca init' (bootstrap workspace with .rorca/ directory). bin/rorca.ts is entry point."

avoid:
  - approach: "Separate routing system for skills (dedicated config.json block, heuristic matching, embedding vectors)."
    reason: "Skills are files — context-router.ts already handles micromatch path scoping + priority + token budgeting. LLM matching piggybacks on spec generation (zero extra cost). Embeddings add latency + infrastructure for negligible accuracy gain over LLM reasoning with MEMORY.md context."
  
  - approach: "Bulk install 30+ skills from skills.sh registry on workspace setup."
    reason: "Context pollution. Token waste. Most skills irrelevant to most stories. LLM-driven per-story matching is selective — only injects relevant skills based on story text + MEMORY.md + AGENTS.md."
  
  - approach: "better-sqlite3 for distribution."
    reason: "Native C++ addon breaks bun build --compile. Switched to PostgreSQL (pure JS pg driver) enables standalone binary compilation AND unlocks vectors/graph (pgvector, Apache AGE)."
  
  - approach: "npm publish for distribution (source code visible in node_modules)."
    reason: "Business model requires source protection. Standalone binary via bun build --compile hides source, no runtime dependency. Install script (curl | sh) downloads binary to /usr/local/bin."
  
  - approach: "Auto-commit runtime state files (.rorca/run-state.json, progress.txt)."
    reason: "Causes merge conflicts during wave-based parallel execution (multiple worktrees writing same files). Added .gitignore patterns — runtime state is ephemeral, not source of truth."
  
  - approach: "Multiple execution engine implementations (run-loop.sh bash variant, run-loop.ts TypeScript variant, execution-engine.ts)."
    reason: "Code duplication. Diverging behavior across agents. Consolidated to execution-engine.ts only — single source of truth for claude, opencode, codex. run-loop.sh kept as bash fallback (only used if execution-engine.ts missing)."
  
  - approach: "Auto-promote skills based on effectiveness analytics (auto-install high-performing skills)."
    reason: "Removes user agency. Show effectiveness data in UI (SkillAnalyticsWidget), let user decide. Explicit > implicit for skill adoption."
```

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Fix rorca_enrich_spec to use the same retrieval pipeline as rorca_generate_spec. The enrich route (POST /api/specs/:id/enrich in backend/src/routes/specs.ts) currently implements its own inline 4-layer retrieval cascade that: selects memories ORDER BY created_at DESC (recency, not relevance), returns the same 10 memories for every story (no per-story cosine similarity), always reports cagHits: 0 (never uses memory-router.ts CAG cache), and has its own hardcoded pgvector/AGE/tsvector/direction-only logic disconnected from memory-router.ts.

The generate route (POST /api/specs/generate) correctly calls retrieveContext(workspaceId, queryText, { maxTokens, includeGraph }) from backend/src/lib/memory-router.ts which does: Step 1 CAG (in-memory cache, 0ms), Step 2 RAG (hybridSearch pgvector cosine + tsvector BM25 RRF hybrid, ~100ms), Step 3 Graph (Apache AGE traversal when includeGraph: true).

The fix: replace the enrich route inline cascade with a call to retrieveContext() per story. Each story gets its own retrieveContext(workspaceId, story.title + story.description, { maxTokens: 2000, includeGraph: true }) call so different stories get semantically different memories matched via cosine similarity. Aggregate cagHits/ragHits/graphHits/latencyMs across all per-story calls. Write context_summary_json to spec_generation_logs using canonical ContextSummary schema (directionLayers, skills, memory: { count, tier, cagHits, ragHits, graphHits, latencyMs }, tokenBudget, flags). retrieval_method column reflects highest tier used. UI: Context tab for enriched specs shows same rich ContextSummaryCard as generated specs.
